summary: Players like it for easy power, control and light, manoeuvrable handling at a good price. Feel divides opinion, with some finding it dry and stiff and others too bouncy. Several report paint chips or cracks, and a few find the sweet spot small.

Players find it manoeuvrable, forgiving and easy on the arm, with good control and a big sweet spot. The main complaint is a soft, trampoline-like feel, worse in warm weather and on blocks, and many want more power on smashes. Several report cracking.

Most players like the large, forgiving sweet spot, easy power and control, and many add weights at the top for more punch. The soft, springy face divides opinion, with some finding it too bouncy at the net or in warm weather. A few report the weight screws breaking.

Players describe a firm, crisp racket with good control, a forgiving sweet spot and quick handling, which many find arm-friendly. Stiffness divides opinion, with some finding it too hard or the sweet spot too small. A few report cracks or chipping paint.

Players praise it for control, manoeuvrability and a gentle effect on the arm, a little more direct than the 18K. It is not a power racket for some, and a few find it dry, stiff or demanding. A few report cracks or chipping paint.

Players describe a control racket with a large, forgiving sweet spot and little trampoline effect, liked for its dry touch and manoeuvrability. Downsides are units heavier than listed, firmness that gave some elbow or arm pain, and smashes needing more effort. Some remove the stock grip to cut weight.

Players value it for control and a crisp, firm, dry feel. The common downsides are heavy, head-heavy handling and arm, elbow or shoulder pain for many, plus a rock-hard feel in cold weather. A few say the rough finish wore off quickly. Suits control players with healthy arms.

Players describe a light, manoeuvrable diamond with strong control, a fairly forgiving sweet spot and good build quality, and many find it easy on the arm. The trade-off is a bit less top-end power. Feel splits opinion, with some finding it too soft and others too stiff.

Players describe it as soft, comfortable and forgiving, with good control and a gentle feel on the arm. The main downsides are modest power and a springy face that gets away from some players at pace. Suits those who want comfort and control over raw pop.

Players like it for easy power and strong smashes, with light units available. The head-heavy balance is the main complaint, making it tiring and harder to defend with, and some got arm pain. A few report cracks or foam noise. Suits technical attackers.

Players find it light, fast and manoeuvrable, strongest at the net, with a stiff, dry feel. The main downside is a small, punishing sweet spot, and the firmness leaves some with arm or shoulder pain. It rewards good technique and is demanding for others.

Most players who like it point to free power, especially on smashes and attacking shots. The downsides are a small sweet spot, a high balance that makes it slower to move and defend with, and arm pain for several. Best suited to strong, advanced attacking players.

Players mostly like it for a very large, forgiving sweet spot, a soft feel, solid defence and kindness to the arm. The main drawback is a strong trampoline effect on blocks and fast volleys, and several report cracking or broken plastic weights. Suits defensive, control-minded players.

Players describe a diamond that handles like a rounder shape, with easy power on overheads, a dry feel and good manoeuvrability. Many find it kind to the arm and fairly forgiving. The head-heavy balance bothers some, and a few struggle with lobs and low balls or report cracking.

Players describe it as dry, firm and manoeuvrable, with strong control, good build quality and little vibration that many find easy on the arm. Some find it demanding with a smaller sweet spot, and the weight and balance often need tuning, with several removing the weight plate.

Players find it light and manoeuvrable with a firm, dry feel, little trampoline effect and good control, with power when needed. Some want more power, off-centre hits die for a few, and a few report chips, cracks or rattles. A few found it bouncy instead.

Players praise it mainly for easy power in attack, but it is demanding. Several find it stiff or hard to control on blocks and off-centre hits, and some got arm or elbow pain. A few report cracking. Suits strong, aggressive players.

Players like the big, forgiving sweet spot, easy control, quick handling and help in defence. Some find the rebound too high or the racket heavy. The glossy paint scratches easily, and a few report cracking.

Most players like its control and forgiving sweet spot, and it is easy on the arm. The usual drawback is modest power, and the springy face sends blocks long for some. A few say it cracked after hard play. A good fit for patient, control-minded players.

Players describe it as powerful, especially on smashes, with a firm, dry feel and good control for those who can handle it. It is demanding, heavy and hard to manoeuvre in defence for many. Several report cracking, sometimes within weeks. Suits strong, technical attackers.

Players are split. Some find a good mix of power and control, with precise placement and quick handling at the net. Several find it demanding, with an unpredictable sweet spot, less smash power than hoped, and little improvement over the Vertex 03. Suits experienced players better than those stepping up.

Most players love the mix of control and power. It feels dry and firm without much trampoline, and is easy to handle. A few find it short on power or hollow, and one unit broke from a defect. Suits players wanting a less bouncy, more controllable racket.

Most players like it: easy to manoeuvre, good control, forgiving for a diamond shape, and comfortable with little vibration. A few felt arm or shoulder pain, or found it firm with a modest sweet spot. Power is decent but not extreme.

Most players love it as an attacking racket: strong ball exit, solid control and a decent sweet spot for a diamond. The main downsides are its weight and stiff feel, which tire some players over long matches and gave one shoulder pain. Suits stronger players.

Most players like it: medium-hard and dry, manoeuvrable, with good control and little trampoline. It is firmer than some rackets and can punish off-centre hits or tire the elbow, and one found the feel dull. Several rate it well against pricier rackets.

Most players like the dry, firm feel with no trampoline, good control and quick handling at the net, especially those coming from bouncier AT10 models. Downsides are a somewhat smaller sweet spot and less forgiveness, and a few reported low balance or surface defects.

Most players like it for being light on the arm, very manoeuvrable and strong in defence and at the net. The soft feel means limited power, especially on overheads and smashes. A good fit for players wanting comfort and speed over punch.

Most players praise its control and precise placement, with light handling and little vibration. The main downsides are limited power and ball output, especially on smashes, and some found it stiff or not forgiving. Suits control-minded players more than beginners.

Players mostly agree it has plenty of power, especially on smashes. The trade-offs are a smaller sweet spot, less forgiveness and extra weight, with several reporting arm pain or control errors in the back court. Suits attackers more than control players.

Most players rate its control and defence highly, with good manoeuvrability and a firmer, dry feel. A few dislike the foam, finding it too soft or lifeless, and some miss power at the net or on off-centre hits. Mostly positive.

Players like the rough face for spin, the weight for smashing, and its durability. The main downsides are a smaller sweet spot that punishes poor contact and a stiff feel that can be demanding, so it suits intermediate players more than beginners.

Players praise its ball speed and smash power, but it is demanding. Several struggled with control, placement and a shrunken sweet spot, and its high balance felt heavy or hard on the elbow. Better for natural hitters than anyone seeking forgiveness.

Players mostly like it for being light and manoeuvrable, with good control, a big sweet spot and solid defence. The main downside is lack of power, especially on overheads. A couple found it too stiff or did not click with the feel.

Light, quick and easy to move, with a crisp, firm feel that most players like at the net and on overheads. The main downsides are a small sweet spot that punishes off-centre hits and a demanding character. Several say it is bigger and more forgiving than the 2025 version, but it suits players with decent technique.

Most players enjoy how it plays, with easy manoeuvrability, solid defence, good power and a gentle feel on the arm. The big problem is durability: many report cracks in the carbon face, loose parts or rattles within a few months. Some who love the racket still call the build quality a deal-breaker.

Players know it mainly for easy, explosive power, with decent control and agility for a power-oriented shape. Some find it head-heavy or heavy, and its firm, dry feel can be demanding on off days. Best for players who want to attack and have the technique to handle it.

Players praise it for control and comfort, with a sweet spot that many find generous and a balanced, fairly firm feel that is kind to the arm. Power is only moderate for some. A few find the sweet spot small or the feel too hard, so it does not suit everyone.

Light, manoeuvrable and punchy, which many players love at the net and for finishing points. The main complaints are a small sweet spot, some trampoline-like inconsistency, and vibration for a couple of players. Several who moved from other rackets are very happy, while others sold it.

A firm, dry racket that most players praise for control, with decent power once adjusted to. Downsides include a small sweet spot where off-centre hits go dead, a head-heavy feel for some, and a demanding character. Better suited to more advanced players.

Players like its manoeuvrability, defence and comfortable, arm-friendly feel, with a dry touch and good all-round play. Some find it head-heavy, a bit short on power or softening over time. Feedback is mixed on the sweet spot, so it suits those wanting a balanced diamond over a big hitter.

Players describe it as very light and manoeuvrable, a favourite at the net, with a stiff feel that several find easy on the arm. The clear downside is a small sweet spot that makes off-centre hits die, and it demands good technique. A few players disagree and find it forgiving.

Players describe a head-heavy diamond that gives plenty of easy power on smashes and volleys. The trade-off is defence, where the weight in the head makes it slower and harder to handle, and some find it demanding. Several remove the side weights to improve balance.

An attacking, high-balance racket that fans praise for its mix of power and control. The main downsides are that it is demanding and head-heavy, which hurts defence for some. A few report elbow or shoulder discomfort, so it suits confident players who commit to each shot.

Players describe a hard, dry, heavy diamond that rewards technique. Fans like its feel, smash power and the control it gives in defence and at the net. Many others find it demanding and unforgiving, with a small sweet spot and poor manoeuvrability. Best for experienced players who want a firm racket.

A powerful, head-heavy diamond that most players enjoy for overheads and volleys, with a firm feel despite the name. Some find it demanding, and a few report paint flaking or the frame breaking. Several say it is easier to handle than the regular Lebrón Viper.

Players mostly praise it for control, with a firm, stable feel and good manoeuvrability. Some find it a little short on power or too dead on blocks, and a few say it feels demanding. A couple of earlier owners found the 2026 firmer than past versions.

A light, dry control racket that players like for its precision and quickness. The main downside is a very firm feel, with a few reporting elbow or wrist discomfort, and it can feel demanding or short on power. Some call it superb, others were not convinced.
